findings.element: Meldungen · ELA (DE) box and its state line, after choosing an item in Quelle = Library / Voice recording
findings.finding: After a library or recording pick the ELA (DE) box can keep showing the previous text while the state line asserts Aus Bibliothek / Mitschrift der Aufnahme and the audio line reports a ready file, so the text on screen is not the text that was loaded or that will be spoken.
findings.user_impact: The dispatcher signs off on a German announcement they can see while a different German text and its audio are what actually go out to the platform loudspeakers.
findings.suggested_fix: On a library/recording pick, write the model text into both textareas unconditionally instead of skipping the one that currently has focus, so the visible text always equals the stored text.

evidence.action: Picked an item in Gespeicherte Meldung and then in Aufnahme after having edited the DE box; compared the DE box, EN box, state lines and audio line in shots 08-library and 09-voice.
evidence.observed: Shot 09: recording r2 is loaded (EN box = [Recording] Please leave the platform., audio = Audio erzeugt 0:22 eine Datei DE + EN) but the DE box still reads the previous generated text under the label Mitschrift der Aufnahme; shot 08 shows the same mismatch under Aus Bibliothek. index.html only writes the textarea when it is not the active element.

findings.element: ELA · Gespeicherte Meldung and Aufnahme dropdowns
findings.finding: Both source pickers fall back to bitte waehlen after a pick, so the panel simultaneously says nothing has been chosen and that the message came from the library / a recording with audio already rendered.
findings.user_impact: The dispatcher cannot tell which approved message or recording is currently loaded, cannot re-check it before sign-off, and is invited to pick again — which reloads and overwrites whatever they have adjusted since.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the chosen option selected in both pickers (emit the selected attribute when the options are rebuilt, as Tonfall already does) so the loaded source item stays named on screen.

evidence.action: Picked a saved message, then a second one, then a recording, and read the control values back.
evidence.observed: value_read_back is empty for both pickers after two picks; shots 08 and 09 show bitte waehlen in the picker while the boxes are badged Aus Bibliothek / Mitschrift der Aufnahme with a green Audio erzeugt line. The option lists are rebuilt on every render without a selected attribute.

findings.element: ELA · ELA GENERIEREN button and the Meldungen state lines during generation
findings.finding: Text generation shows no progress of any kind — only the words Wird generiert repeated as placeholder and state line — and the button stays enabled throughout, while the audio render right below it does show a determinate progress bar and disables its controls.
findings.user_impact: With no sign that anything is moving, dispatchers under time pressure click ELA GENERIEREN again (KF-1); each extra click silently swaps in a different variant with no way back to the wording they had.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable ELA GENERIEREN while a generation is in flight and show the same determinate progress treatment the audio render already uses, plus a way to step back to the previous variant.

evidence.action: Clicked ELA GENERIEREN once and then three more times, inspecting the loading state (shot 03) and the repeat behaviour.
evidence.observed: loading_state records any_spinner_or_progress 0 and button_still_enabled_during_generation true; shot 03 shows only grey Wird generiert text. Repeat clicks cycle 3 distinct variants with no way back, while the audio loading state records progress_bar 1 and listen_enabled_during_render false.

findings.element: Meldungen · ELA (EN) box while flagged Uebersetzung nicht aktuell
findings.finding: Typing anything into the EN box clears the out-of-date-translation warning and relabels the box Manuell bearbeitet without any check that EN now matches DE.
findings.user_impact: The one signal that the two halves of the announcement have drifted apart disappears the moment the dispatcher touches the field, so a pair that says different things reads as fully in order and both halves go out on the same audio file.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the divergence flag until the EN text is re-derived from the current DE text, or until the dispatcher explicitly confirms the pair as checked, rather than clearing it on the first keystroke.

evidence.action: Appended a sentence to ELA (DE) to raise the warning (shot 05), then typed into ELA (EN).
evidence.observed: EN state line changes from Uebersetzung nicht aktuell (amber, box outlined) to Manuell bearbeitet; the state map records warning_cleared_by_editing_en true and no_check_that_the_two_languages_still_match true.

findings.element: Audio · waveform block to the right of ANHOEREN / STOP
findings.finding: The waveform next to the play button looks like a scrubber but is purely decorative, renders identically for fresh, stale, library and recording audio, and nothing indicates position or remaining time while the file plays.
findings.user_impact: Dispatchers click the waveform to jump to the English half or replay a phrase and get a dead click (KF-4), and during a 16-22 second bilingual file they cannot tell whether it is still playing, stuck, or finished.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the waveform a real position indicator that advances during playback, or render it as a flat non-interactive graphic and add an elapsed/total time readout next to STOP.

evidence.action: Generated audio, clicked ANHOEREN, and compared the audio zone across shots 06 fresh, 07 stale, 08 library and 09 recording.
evidence.observed: The state map records waveform_is_decorative_not_a_scrubber true and no_progress_indication_while_playing true; the only feedback on play is the label flipping to STOP and angehoert appended to the state line, and the waveform glyph is identical in all four states including Audio veraltet.

gaps: Aufnahme picker: the state map records value_read_back empty, so what a recording pick commits into a visible, unfocused DE box was never observed — UX-1 is grounded in the EN box, the audio duration and the render code, not in a clean unfocused pick.
Audio failure recovery: Sprachdienst nicht erreichbar was reached, but AUDIO ERZEUGEN was never pressed again with the failure switched off, so whether retrying clears the error line is unknown.

Angehoert semantics: the listened flag is set the instant ANHOEREN is pressed rather than when playback ends, and real TTS playback was never exercised, so whether the save check reflects the dispatcher actually hearing the file is unverified.
A fourth EN warning branch exists in the code (Zusatztext not translated) but no state in the map reaches it, so its wording and whether it can be cleared the same way as UX-4 are unknown.

Concurrent warnings: the save line renders one message at a time in a fixed priority order, but no state combined two problems, so whether a dispatcher with a too-long DAISY text is ever shown the stale-audio warning was not observed.
